rationale: I read the complete held EO 9204 original (7 FR 5657): sections 1-3 designate the Secretary of the Interior as Fishery Coordinator, create and define the functions of the Office of Fishery Coordination and authorize staffing; section 4 makes it effective July 21, 1942 and continuing 'so long as Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941, remains in force'. I read the held official FR text of EO 9649 (October 29, 1945): 'The Office of Fishery Coordination ... established pursuant to Executive Order No. 9204 of July 21, 1942, together with the office of Fishery Coordinator, is terminated', with direction to wind up its affairs. Every institution EO 9204 creates or designates is terminated, so the order has no remaining function; it is not named as revoked, and that gap is stated. I used only the FR-text ACTOR record, not the APP-derived ACT copy, as the basis. No savings clause beyond winding up; EO 9204's war-powers term ran out independently when Title I of the First War Powers Act lapsed. Catalog 'See: EO 9649' and 1989 snapshot are leads. Provisional NO hypothesis; exact legal end remains a lifecycle gap.
lifecycle_gaps_retained: No complete machine later-source search available.

EO 9649 terminates the Office and the office of Fishery Coordinator without naming EO 9204 as revoked; the own term (continues while Title I of the First War Powers Act remains in force) is a second possible end.
